options.text: the supreme law-making power of a state within its territory
the total population living within a defined territory
the machinery through which state decisions are carried out
the written document that establishes the organs of government

questions.explanation: Sovereignty is about finality: it is the authority that no other body inside the state can overrule, together with freedom from outside dictation. It is the element that turns a mere territory into a state.

distractorRationale.b: Population is a separate element of statehood
distractorRationale.c: That describes government, which is only the agent of the sovereign state
distractorRationale.d: That describes a constitution, which regulates how sovereignty is exercised

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an element of a state?
questions.explanation: The four elements of a state are population, defined territory, government and sovereignty. A written constitution is not required: the United Kingdom is a fully sovereign state without one.

distractorRationale.a: Without people there is no political community to govern
distractorRationale.b: A state must have boundaries within which its authority runs
distractorRationale.d: Sovereignty is the element that distinguishes a state from a colony or a local council

questions.stem: In Nigeria, political sovereignty is said to reside in
questions.explanation: Legal sovereignty belongs to the body empowered to enact law, but political sovereignty belongs to the voters who decide who occupies that body. This is the practical meaning of popular sovereignty.

distractorRationale.a: The National Assembly holds legal sovereignty, exercised within the Constitution
distractorRationale.c: The Supreme Court interprets the law; it does not create the mandate to make it
distractorRationale.d: The President exercises executive power derived from the electorate's mandate

questions.stem: The main difference between a state and a nation is that a state

options.text: is always larger in population than a nation
possesses sovereignty, while a nation is a people bound by common identity
must have a single language, while a nation may have many
is temporary, while a nation is permanent

questions.explanation: A state is a legal and political entity defined by sovereignty over a territory; a nation is a cultural and psychological entity defined by shared identity. Nigeria is one state containing many nations, which is why it is called a multi-national state.

distractorRationale.a: Some nations, such as the Igbo, outnumber the populations of many small states
distractorRationale.c: Many sovereign states, Nigeria included, have hundreds of languages
distractorRationale.d: Governments are temporary; the state itself is permanent

questions.stem: A military government that controls the machinery of state after a coup but has no constitutional basis is said to exercise
questions.explanation: De facto means in fact: the regime actually commands obedience even though the law does not authorise it. De jure sovereignty, by contrast, is what the law recognises.

distractorRationale.a: De jure sovereignty requires legal recognition, which an unconstitutional seizure lacks
distractorRationale.c: External sovereignty concerns independence from other states, not internal legality
distractorRationale.d: Delegated sovereignty describes powers passed down to subordinate bodies

questions.stem: Which of the following most clearly limits the sovereignty of a modern state in practice?

options.text: The existence of many ethnic groups within its borders
Treaty obligations undertaken as a member of international organisations
Periodic changes of government through elections
The delegation of functions to local government councils

questions.explanation: By ratifying treaties a state binds itself to act in ways it would otherwise be free to reject, and bodies such as the United Nations, the African Union and ECOWAS can lawfully call it to account. That is a genuine external restraint on an otherwise absolute power.

distractorRationale.a: Ethnic diversity may complicate governing but does not reduce the state's legal supremacy
distractorRationale.c: Changes of government leave sovereignty untouched, because sovereignty belongs to the state
distractorRationale.d: Delegating functions distributes the exercise of sovereignty internally without limiting the sovereign itself

questions.stem: Colonial Nigeria before 1960 was a sovereign state.
questions.explanation: False. Colonial Nigeria had population, territory and a government, but final authority rested with Britain, so the fourth element of statehood was missing. Sovereignty was attained at independence on 1 October 1960.

distractorRationale.a: Having a government is not the same as having supreme authority; the Governor-General answered to London

questions.stem: The attribute of sovereignty which means that it continues to exist even when a particular government falls is
questions.explanation: Sovereignty belongs to the state, not to whoever happens to be in office, so it survives coups, elections and resignations. This is why Nigeria's treaties and debts bind each succeeding administration.

distractorRationale.b: Indivisibility means sovereignty cannot be split into parts
distractorRationale.c: Exclusiveness means only one sovereign may exist in a territory
distractorRationale.d: Universality means sovereignty covers every person and association in the territory
